cohort: 77 patients who had given birth prematurely at 24.0-36.6 weeks gestation, or who had undergone fetal fibronectin testing between January 1, 2015 and December 31, 2015 at Metropolitan Hospital, NYC Health+Hospitals, New York
finding: In a low-risk population presenting with symptoms of preterm labor, fetal fibronectin testing did not improve clinical outcomes and was associated with higher rates of hospital admissions and steroid administration.
